summary.headline: Kirloskar Brothers Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% YoY to Rs.11,049 million, but EBITDA grew only 2% at an 11.8% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to Rs.11,049 million and consolidated EBITDA rose 2% to Rs.1,306 million, a margin of 11.8%. Standalone domestic revenue grew 9% to Rs.6,738 million, EBITDA 16% to Rs.920 million, and PAT 15% to Rs.540 million. International revenue grew 19%, but international EBITDA margin fell to 5.1% on lower high-margin services revenue at SPP UK and weak Rodelta execution. Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27 on both standalone and consolidated bases, while acknowledging that a large order slipped and foundry modernisation delayed some dispatches.

financial_highlights.change: driven by SPP USA and Kirloskar Brothers Thailand
moderated due to lower services contribution

segments.name: Standalone domestic (KBL)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs.6,738 million (+9%), EBITDA Rs.920 million (+16%), PAT Rs.540 million (+15%). Domestic pending order book Rs.25,577 million excluding small pump order book.

segments.name: International (overseas)
segments.commentary: Revenue +19% YoY, led by SPP USA and KBT Thailand. EBITDA Rs.207 million at 5.1% margin. Overseas pending order book Rs.15,045 million.

segments.name: SPP USA
segments.commentary: Growing 20-plus% in the quarter, driven by data centers, fire and HVAC projects; a multi-year framework with a large US data center operator is near signing (under NDA).

segments.name: SPP UK / Rodelta (Netherlands)
segments.commentary: SPP UK margin pressure from lower services revenue as chemical/petrochemical service contracts idled; management expects services recovery from Q2 FY27 for SPP UK and Q3 for KBL. Rodelta losses widened on delayed execution; improvement expected over the next two quarters.

segments.name: KPML (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Margin fell from 12.5% to 7.3% after merger of loss-making TKSL (steel castings) into KPML; management expects TKSL to turn profitable.

guidance_outlook: Double-digit revenue growth in FY27 over FY26 for standalone business, reiterated.
Management will strive for double-digit consolidated revenue growth in FY27.
Services business expected to recover from Q2 FY27 at SPP UK and from Q3 at KBL, lifting blended overseas margins.
Rodelta execution expected to improve over the next two quarters; all entities expected to be profitable with better-than-prior-year numbers.
About two-thirds of the domestic order board (~Rs.2,500 crore) expected to execute in FY27.
Capex expected to be roughly equal to depreciation, focused on modernisation, debottlenecking and quality.
Management asks investors to assess performance half-yearly or annually rather than quarterly.
capex_capacity: Foundry modernisation programme completed; management says it will enable higher revenues and faster execution, though it delayed some dispatches in Q1.
Capex guided at roughly equal to depreciation for FY27, mainly modernisation, debottlenecking and quality.
Nuclear primary circuit pump development is close to order placement; metallurgical trials in European and Indian foundries expected to conclude by mid-to-late August.
Pump-based IoT devices now in second version; deployed base is in the hundreds in India.
demand_pricing: Standalone order intake grew about 5.4% YoY per management's corrected figure; consolidated order intake +4% to Rs.13,954 million. A large order was delayed into later quarters.
Price increases of about 10% taken since January, which management says is sufficient to cover raw material cost increases; gross margin improved on product mix and price.
Oil and gas: petrol pump order booking of about Rs.217 crore cumulative to Q1-end; Rs.74 crore dispatched in the quarter.
Power order book grew about 30%; nuclear primary circuit pump orders of about Rs.70 crore and secondary circuit orders of about Rs.40 crore received in Q1.
Industry order book was Rs.1,497 million (the Rs.556 million figure quoted was marine & defence), per the corrected print.
Data centres: hyperscale package USD7.5-10 million excluding intake water system; about 4,000 operating US data centres plus 2,000 with planning permission.

qa_highlights.question: Why are inventories and advances rising and is dispatch being withheld, hindering double-digit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory built up during the foundry upgrade, which is now complete; some orders were half-finished, so full shipments slipped. Improvement was seen in the current month and is expected in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: When will the services expansion lift SPP UK margins, and what is the outlook for Rodelta?
qa_highlights.answer: SPP UK services expected to restart in Q2 FY27 (Q3 for KBL) as power plant and water utility contracts ramp. Rodelta delays are due to consolidating Dutch entities; improvement expected in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why was consolidated margin down from 13% in Q4 to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said standalone EBITDA margin was 13.7% vs 12.8% last year; the drop was mainly SPP UK. Management agreed margins should recover as services revive from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the domestic order book executes in FY27, and what drove the power order book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds of the ~Rs.2,500 crore domestic order book expected in FY27. Power growth is largely nuclear, with primary and secondary circuit orders received in Q1 and new thermal plants.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the KPML margin fall from 12.5% to 7.3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to the merger of loss-making TKSL into KPML; management expects TKSL to turn profitable on BHEL and KBL demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is normally equal to depreciation, used for modernisation, debottlenecking and quality. No specific figure was given.

risks_watch: Inventory and advances rising sharply (per annual report, inventory WIP 180 to 241; advances Rs.32 crore to Rs.91 crore) with dispatch timing dependent on customers accepting goods.
Overseas EBITDA margin at 5.1%; recovery depends on SPP UK services contracts and Rodelta execution over the next two quarters.
Finance cost up 31% and other expenses up 21% YoY; other expenses rising from digitalisation and advertising spend.
Large order delays (domestic orders, petrol pump dispatch subject to end-customer acceptance) make quarterly numbers lumpy.
Nuclear primary circuit pump metallurgical qualification and tender outcome expected within weeks.
